title: Network Telemetry Stack
description: Mermaid layered diagram of five network telemetry sources (full PCAP, application logs, firewall/proxy logs, NetFlow/IPFIX, DNS logs) ordered by fidelity and coverage, all feeding a SIEM / data lake, with a cost trade-off note.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: Advanced Network Defense: Wireless, DNS, and Zero Trust

educational.topic: Network security monitoring data sources and the fidelity/coverage/cost trade-off
learningObjectives: Identify the five common network telemetry sources and the question each one answers.
Compare the sources along the fidelity, coverage, and storage-cost dimensions.
Explain why teams keep cheap broad telemetry always-on and high-fidelity capture on-demand.
educational.prerequisites: Basic networking and the idea of logging and a SIEM.

controls: Read the five layers top (high fidelity) to bottom (broad coverage)
Each layer shows data type, example tool, and the question it answers
Fidelity axis (up) and Coverage axis (down) flank the diagram
pedagogical.assessment: Students place a given investigative question (e.g., 'what bytes were sent?') at the correct telemetry layer and justify the storage trade-off.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing full packet capture should be retained for everything.
Assuming high-fidelity data also has the broadest coverage.
